input.justification: The HTTP parameter "BenchmarkTest01329" is read from request.getParameterMap(), passed through an inner class method (Test.doSomething) that merely stores/retrieves it from a List with no validation or sanitization, and the resulting value (bar) is concatenated directly into a path string used to build a java.net.URI and then a java.io.File object. There is no path canonicalization, whitelist check, or removal of "../" sequences anywhere in the flow. The ESAPI encodeForHTML call is only applied when printing the resulting file path to the HTTP response (output encoding for XSS), not before using the tainted data to construct the File object, so it does not mitigate path traversal. Hence user input can control the file path passed to the file system, which is a genuine path/file injection vulnerability.
